newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia policeman dies in right-wing attack.
newsitem.headline: Colombia policeman dies in right-wing attack.

text.p: Suspected right-wing paramilitary fighters shot and killed a policeman on Friday in a failed bid to blow up the Bogota headquarters of a radical leftist political party, authorities said.

The policeman, who was guarding the offices of the Patriotic Union (UP) party, died after a pre-dawn shoot out with three men he discovered planting a bomb made of 23 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite, a police spokesman said.

Sebastian Gonzalez, UP secretary general, said the party began receiving threats a few weeks ago from a right-wing death-squad, the so-called "Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba" (ACCU), which targets those it accuses of links to leftist rebels.
"We received threats a month ago that they were going to dynamite the headquarters in Bogota but still we could only get one guard armed with just a pistol," Gonzalez told Reuters.
The UP was set up as a legitimate party in 1985 as the result of failed peace talks with Latin America's largest and oldest guerrilla army, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
Critics charge that the UP -- with one senator and about 130 city council seats nationwide -- is a political front for the FARC.
